# Mercatus Liber

> "Free market" (Latin). A legitimate, 100% free/open-source alternative to Shopify/Medusa/
> Saleor/etc. -- headless, AI-agent-accessible, and built to be stood up with a single tool.
> (README.md, lines 1-4.)

A free, MIT-licensed, headless commerce framework: a schema-first product/SKU catalog with
pluggable database adapters, a marketing catalog genuinely separate from the sales catalog (the
gap no existing free/OSS commerce platform actually fills), a per-page CMS instead of forced
whole-site theming, a long-lived cart, adapter-based payments (Stripe first), analytics on by
default (PostHog, config-swappable), and a plugin system for everything else (OMS, fulfillment,
notifications). (README.md, "A free, MIT-licensed..." paragraph.)

Built as an AI *and* human commerce tool from the ground up -- every capability exposed to a
human storefront/admin UI is equally exposed to AI agents via a documented skills/tool catalog
and an MCP server, calling the exact same subsystem interfaces. No shadow API, no reduced
agent-only surface. (README.md, "AI and human commerce tool" paragraph.)

Not a hosted SaaS platform: the goal is something a small business, an agency, or an individual
developer can pick up, self-host or deploy anywhere, and own outright -- no per-transaction cut,
no forced app-store tax, no vendor lock-in. Status: pre-alpha, under active development.
License: MIT. Give it away. (VISION.md, opening paragraph; README.md "Status"/"License" lines.)

## Site

- [Framework landing page](https://commerce.mdostal.com/): what Mercatus Liber is, why it exists,
  and links out to the live demos below -- the human-facing equivalent of this file.

## Docs

- [Documentation site](https://mercatus-liber-docs.vercel.app/): narrative, example-driven docs
  (architecture, every subsystem, feature deep-dives, the full planning corpus, and the vision/
  roadmap), built from this repo's own docs/ with Nextra. Currently served from Vercel's own
  subdomain; a custom domain binding remains a future operational step, not a blocker.
  The app itself resolves this URL from the `NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCS_URL` environment variable at
  deploy time (see `app/(landing)/layout.tsx`).

## Demos

Three genuinely separate, simultaneously-live storefronts built on this framework, all under one
deployment via path-based routing (`/demo/<slug>`):

- [The Print Shop](https://commerce.mdostal.com/demo/print-shop): embroidery, custom prints, and
  coasters, opens on the `editorial` theme by default. (VISION.md, "Three demo stores with real
  depth" section.)
- [Northline Home Tech](https://commerce.mdostal.com/demo/northline): a smart-home installer, 4
  categories, 8 real service-area location pages, tiered service SKUs, opens on the `northline`
  theme by default. (VISION.md, same section.)
- [Broadleaf & Co.](https://commerce.mdostal.com/demo/broadleaf): an eclectic artisan/handmade-
  goods shop across Plants, Ceramics & Planters, Textiles & Fiber Arts, and Paper & Ephemera,
  opens on the `vibrant` theme by default. (VISION.md, same section.)
